paras: The killing of Robert Chun was the reported fatal shooting of a Black man by a policeman in Birmingham, Alabama, on the morning of September 2, 1888. Accused of taking goods from a dry goods store, Chun fled from several policemen and was shot at by Policeman Oldham, and a Memphis paper reported the episode under the headline "Killed a Fleeing Burglar."

According to a special dispatch from Birmingham, at about 9 o'clock that morning Chun was found in an alley at the back of "a prominent dry goods store," hooking goods with a wire hook through a window he had broken. Several policemen chased him through the business part of the town to a "negro settlement on the south side." There Policeman Oldham found him hiding under a house, and when Chun ran again the officer fired a 38-caliber pistol at him. The surviving text of the dispatch breaks off at that point, so the account of his death rests on its headline alone.
The coverage does not show an inquest, any inquiry into the shooting, or any report on Chun beyond his name and race.

The only report found ran on September 3, 1888, on page 5 of the Memphis Appeal, as a special dispatch dated Birmingham, September 2. Its headline, "Killed a Fleeing Burglar," named Chun a burglar and tied his death to his flight, and the dispatch gave the police account as fact without any other version. It identified Chun only as "a negro man" and did not say whether he died at the scene.
No local Birmingham report, reprint, or follow-up story was found.
